task: Find out why the ingest service intermittently times out.

messages.content: The ingest service times out a few times an hour in production. Can you find out why? Logs are under logs/ingest/.
I'll start by listing the log files and checking their sizes.

logs/ingest/ingest-2026-10-19.log  48M
logs/ingest/ingest-2026-10-20.log  51M
logs/ingest/ingest-2026-10-21.log  49M
Searching the most recent log for timeout errors.

2026-10-21T03:12:44Z ERROR worker-3 request 8f2a timed out after 30.0s (stage=enrich)
2026-10-21T03:41:09Z ERROR worker-1 request 91bc timed out after 30.0s (stage=enrich)
2026-10-21T04:15:52Z ERROR worker-3 request a03d timed out after 30.0s (stage=enrich)
2026-10-21T05:02:17Z ERROR worker-2 request b7e1 timed out after 30.0s (stage=enrich)
2026-10-21T05:48:30Z ERROR worker-3 request c4f0 timed out after 30.0s (stage=enrich)
2026-10-21T06:20:03Z ERROR worker-1 request d19a timed out after 30.0s (stage=enrich)
Every timeout is in the 'enrich' stage. Let me look at what that stage does.

def enrich(record):
    geo = geo_client.lookup(record.ip)
    org = org_client.lookup(record.account_id)
    record.geo = geo
    record.org = org
    return record
Two external lookups, both synchronous. I'll check the latency of each client around one of the timeouts.

2026-10-21T03:12:14Z DEBUG geo_client lookup 10.4.2.19 took 0.041s
2026-10-21T03:12:14Z DEBUG org_client lookup acct_2291 started
2026-10-21T03:12:44Z WARN org_client lookup acct_2291 no response after 30.0s
The org lookup is the one hanging. I'll check whether particular accounts are involved.

acct_2291  14 timeouts
acct_0087   1 timeout
acct_3310   1 timeout
Most timeouts come from one account, acct_2291. Let me look at the org service's handling of that account.
acct_2291: org_members=48211, last_synced=2026-08-02
acct_2291 has 48,211 members. I'll check how the org service loads members.

def get_org(account_id):
    org = db.query(Org).filter_by(account_id=account_id).one()
    org.members = db.query(Member).filter_by(org_id=org.id).all()
    return org
The org service loads every member on each lookup, but enrich only uses the org name and tier. For large orgs this takes longer than the 30s timeout.

EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT * FROM member WHERE org_id = 7712;
Seq Scan on member  (cost=0.00..91822.10 rows=48211) (actual time=0.03..31604.55)
Planning Time: 0.112 ms
Execution Time: 31688.902 ms
Confirmed: a sequential scan of about 31.7 seconds, with no index on member.org_id.
Great, what do you recommend?

Two changes. First, add an index on member.org_id, which should bring this query well under a second. Second, add a lightweight get_org_summary endpoint that returns only name and tier, and have enrich call that instead. The index fixes the immediate timeouts; the endpoint stops enrich depending on member counts at all. I'd also add a metric for org_client latency per account so this is visible next time.
